article_title: Teaching Prompt-Based Programming with LLMs: A 45-Minute Lesson with Guided Practice for End-User Programmers
citation: Keith Tran, Samiha Marwan, and Thomas Price. (2026). Teaching Prompt-Based Programming with LLMs: A 45-Minute Lesson with Guided Practice for End-User Programmers. https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.30547
title: 45-minute prompt-based programming lesson with guided practice for end-user programmers
description: A lightweight lesson integrating selected CS1/CS2 concepts (function structure, data transformation, edge cases) with LLM prompting strategies, designed via backward design to fit a single class period. It consisted of "5 short sections (˜5 minutes each)", one per learning objective, each followed by active learning activities including live demonstrations and 3 Promptly problems with automated feedback. All instructional materials are publicly available, and the lesson requires no prior CS background.
requirements: Delivered as a single 45-minute class period with lecture, slides, and Promptly practice problems with automated feedback
No prior CS background required for learners
constraints: Focused exclusively on prompting skills, with no instruction in Python syntax or code comprehension
Designed for end-user programmers such as first-year engineering students
target_learners: first-year engineering students without formal CS coursework
examples: Students practiced filtering words by length while the corresponding test item required filtering numbers by range, to assess transfer
